title: UPS Battery Health
exclusions: Does not cover unmanaged UPS hardware lacking SNMP endpoints, proprietary MIB variants whose counters lack parity with UPS-MIB semantics, or predictive cell chemistry modeling beyond polled SNMP gauges referenced here.
evidence: The savedsearches.conf stanza for the UPS battery alert (schedule, time range, throttling), the triggered-alert history for the audit period, and for each alerted ups_name the matching snmp:ups rows plus the card's battery status page or event-log export showing the same charge, runtime or replace-battery state.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Index three snmp:ups events into index=power within 15 minutes: ups_name=UPS-A1 with charge_pct=72, runtime_min=22, battery_replace_indicator="no"; ups_name=UPS-B2 with charge_pct=100, runtime_min=11, battery_replace_indicator="no"; ups_name=UPS-C3 with charge_pct=98, runtime_min=40, battery_replace_indicator="yes". Run the search over the last 15 minutes and expect exactly three rows, one per UPS (low charge, low runtime, replace flag).
controlTest.negativeScenario: Index two snmp:ups events into index=power for ups_name=UPS-D4: charge_pct=96, runtime_min=38, battery_replace_indicator="no", battery_status="normal", and charge_pct=80, runtime_min=15, battery_replace_indicator="no" (exactly on both thresholds). Run the search and expect zero rows, because the comparisons are strict (< 80, < 15).

dataSources: SNMP polling of each UPS network management card into index=power with sourcetype=snmp:ups. RFC 1628 UPS-MIB supplies charge_pct (upsEstimatedChargeRemaining, 1.3.6.1.2.1.33.1.2.4), runtime_min (upsEstimatedMinutesRemaining, 1.3.6.1.2.1.33.1.2.3) and battery_status (upsBatteryStatus, 1.3.6.1.2.1.33.1.2.1: 1 unknown, 2 normal, 3 low, 4 depleted). UPS-MIB has no replace-battery flag and no battery age: battery_replace_indicator comes from a vendor MIB (APC PowerNet-MIB upsAdvBatteryReplaceIndicator, 1.3.6.1.4.1.318.1.1.1.2.2.4, where 2 = batteryNeedsReplacing, normalised to "yes"), and battery_age_months is derived from APC upsBasicBatteryLastReplaceDate or a CMDB lookup. ups_name and location come from sysName and sysLocation or the same lookup. Collector: SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase 1537) on a heavy forwarder, or Splunk Connect for SNMP (Splunkbase 6266) with its output routed to this index and sourcetype.
spl:
index=power sourcetype="snmp:ups"
| where battery_replace_indicator="yes" OR charge_pct < 80 OR runtime_min < 15
| table ups_name, location, battery_status, charge_pct, runtime_min, battery_age_months
description: Lists every snmp:ups poll in index=power where a UPS reports that its battery needs replacing, its estimated charge is below 80%, or its estimated runtime is below 15 minutes. Each breaching poll becomes one row with ups_name, location, battery_status, charge_pct, runtime_min and battery_age_months. The search does not aggregate per UPS, so a 15-minute window can return up to three rows for the same unit.
value: Finds worn-out or exhausted UPS batteries while utility power is still on, so they can be replaced before the next outage turns a short power blip into a hard shutdown of every rack behind that UPS.
implementation: Poll every UPS management card every 5 minutes for the UPS-MIB battery objects plus the vendor replace-battery flag, and normalise them into index=power sourcetype=snmp:ups using the field names the search expects (map APC upsAdvBatteryReplaceIndicator 2 to "yes"). Schedule the search every 5 minutes over the last 15 minutes. A single breaching poll is enough to alert; if you want consecutive-poll logic, add per-UPS aggregation to the search.
visualization: Primary dashboard row: dual-axis timechart overlaying runtime_min and charge_pct split by ups_name with fifteen-minute spans for smoothing; companion statistic panels for fleet minimum runtime and count of UPS assets breaching thresholds; detail drilldown table sorted ascending on runtime_min with color ranges for battery_status; optional choropleth or rack-floor SVG only when CMDB supplies coordinates.
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable — no CIM data model covers UPS battery telemetry, so the search runs on raw snmp:ups events. If search load matters, a metrics index (with mstats) or a summary index are options; neither is data model acceleration.

references.title: Splunk Connect for SNMP — Splunk configuration (default indexes)

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Recharge after an outage or self-test** — after running on battery, charge_pct stays below 80 for several hours while the batteries recharge on snmp:ups. Distinguish it with upsSecondsOnBattery (non-zero or recently reset) or the card's last-transfer event in the same window, and suppress the UPS until charge recovers.
2. **Load growth, not battery wear** — runtime_min drops below 15 when IT load behind the UPS rises, even with healthy batteries. Compare upsOutputPercentLoad with the previous week; a load step with normal battery_status points to capacity planning, not battery replacement.
3. **Runtime calibration** — a scheduled runtime calibration deliberately discharges the battery, so charge and runtime fall for the duration of the test. Match the alert time against the calibration schedule in the card's event log.
4. **Maintenance and bypass** — during battery replacement or when the UPS is in bypass, cards can report runtime 0 or a stale replace flag. Suppress UPS units listed in your maintenance-window lookup (for example ups_maintenance_windows.csv, a local convention keyed on ups_name with start and end times) for the window.

**Suppression mechanism:** a maintenance-window lookup keyed on ups_name, applied before the where clause, plus alert throttling on ups_name.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• A network management card (for example APC NMC2/NMC3, Eaton Gigabit Network Card, Vertiv IntelliSlot) on every UPS, reachable on UDP/161 from the collector, with SNMPv3 authPriv credentials (or a read-only v2c community restricted to the collector's IP in the card's SNMP access list).
• One collector:
  – SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase 1537) on a heavy forwarder, which writes events straight into index=power with sourcetype=snmp:ups; or
  – Splunk Connect for SNMP (Splunkbase 6266), which is not a forwarder add-on. It runs as a containerised service (microk8s or Docker Compose) and sends to Splunk over HEC. By default polled numeric values land in the metrics index netmetrics (sourcetype sc4snmp:metric) and events in netops (sourcetype sc4snmp:event), so the event search in this UC returns nothing until you route its UPS profile to index=power with sourcetype=snmp:ups, or rewrite the search with mstats against the metrics index.
• The index power and a role for the facilities team (for example power_ops, a local role) with search access to it.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Poll these objects every 5 minutes. RFC 1628 UPS-MIB, which every card implements: upsBatteryStatus (1.3.6.1.2.1.33.1.2.1), upsEstimatedMinutesRemaining (.2.3), upsEstimatedChargeRemaining (.2.4) and, for false-positive triage, upsSecondsOnBattery (.2.2) and upsOutputPercentLoad (1.3.6.1.2.1.33.1.4.4.1.5). Vendor MIB for the replace flag and battery date, for APC PowerNet-MIB: upsAdvBatteryReplaceIndicator (1.3.6.1.4.1.318.1.1.1.2.2.4) and upsBasicBatteryLastReplaceDate (1.3.6.1.4.1.318.1.1.1.2.1.3). Other vendors expose equivalents in their own MIBs; without one, battery_replace_indicator stays empty and only the charge and runtime thresholds can fire.
Normalise the raw varbinds to the field names the search uses. The left-hand names depend on how your collector labels varbinds, so check one raw event first:
```
# props.conf on the search head
[snmp:ups]
FIELDALIAS-ups_gauges = upsEstimatedChargeRemaining AS charge_pct upsEstimatedMinutesRemaining AS runtime_min
EVAL-battery_status = case(upsBatteryStatus=="1","unknown", upsBatteryStatus=="2","normal", upsBatteryStatus=="3","low", upsBatteryStatus=="4","depleted")
EVAL-battery_replace_indicator = if(upsAdvBatteryReplaceIndicator=="2" OR upsAdvBatteryReplaceIndicator=="batteryNeedsReplacing", "yes", "no")
```
Derive battery_age_months from upsBasicBatteryLastReplaceDate (mm/dd/yy on APC cards) or a CMDB lookup keyed on ups_name, and take ups_name and location from sysName and sysLocation or the same lookup.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Save the search below as a scheduled alert running every 5 minutes (cron */5 * * * *) over earliest=-15m latest=now, so each run covers about three polls.
```spl
index=power sourcetype="snmp:ups"
| where battery_replace_indicator="yes" OR charge_pct < 80 OR runtime_min < 15
| table ups_name, location, battery_status, charge_pct, runtime_min, battery_age_months
```
Every breaching poll becomes its own row: one dip alerts, and a UPS can appear up to three times per run. Throttle the alert on ups_name (for example suppress for 1 hour) to avoid repeat pages. The search does not test battery_status, so a card that reports batteryLow (3) or batteryDepleted (4) while charge and runtime still look healthy is not caught; extending the search to cover that is a human-reviewed SPL change.

Step 3 — Validate
Pick one UPS and compare against the NMC web UI battery status page at the same poll time: charge_pct must equal the card's battery capacity percentage, runtime_min its runtime remaining, and battery_replace_indicator must read "yes" only when the card shows a replace-battery alarm. Run snmpget against the card for the same OIDs to confirm the collector is not truncating or rescaling values.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Route alerts to facilities on-call with ups_name and location. Replace-battery rows go into the battery replacement queue. Low-runtime rows on a UPS that is not on battery usually mean load growth and need a capacity review rather than a battery swap. Put the runtime_min and charge_pct trend per ups_name on the facilities dashboard.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• No snmp:ups events at all with Splunk Connect for SNMP: the data is probably in netmetrics or netops. Search index=netmetrics or index=netops for the UPS IP before changing anything else.
• Polls time out while snmpwalk from another host works: the card's SNMP access list does not include the collector's IP, or SNMPv3 credentials and the engine ID changed after a card firmware update.
• battery_replace_indicator is always "no" or empty: the vendor MIB is not loaded on the collector, or the card is not an APC model; confirm the raw field name in one event.
• battery_age_months is empty: the CMDB lookup has no row for that ups_name, or the card's last-replace date was never set after the last battery swap.
• runtime_min reads 0 or jumps after maintenance: the UPS is in bypass, or a runtime calibration has just finished. Check the card's event log before acting.
